registry.description: Wrath is the settled, purposeful anger of God against everything that corrupts, destroys, and opposes his good creation — not a loss of temper but the moral seriousness of one who will not let evil go unaddressed forever. The Hebrew vocabulary here is spare but intense. Wrath in Scripture is not God's most fundamental attitude toward humanity (love is) but it is his uncompromising response to sin. The gospel addresses wrath directly: what is owed is met, what threatened is turned away, and the wrath that would have fallen is received by the Son.
